parts.title: Meet my robot
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last year, I built my first robot with my father. It took us three months, working every weekend in the garage. It looks a bit like a small dog, with four wheels and two cameras instead of eyes. I called it Pixel.

At first, nothing worked. Pixel could not move in a straight line, and it kept running into the wall. My father said that we should not give up, because every mistake teaches you something. He was right. We changed the program, and after a week, Pixel could follow me around the garden.

Now it can do much more. It can carry my school bag, and it can take pictures when I tell it to. My little brother loves it and wants to teach it to play football. Unfortunately, Pixel is not very good at that, and last week it knocked over a flowerpot.

One day, I would like to build a robot that helps people who cannot walk. I know it will be difficult, but I have already started reading about it. My father says that if I keep working hard, I may be able to do it by the age of twenty.

questions.explanation: It took three months, working every weekend.

options: It could not go in a straight line

questions.explanation: Pixel could not move in a straight line.

options: They cost a lot of money
questions.explanation: Every mistake teaches you something.

questions.explanation: It can carry my school bag.

options: Build a robot for people who cannot walk
questions.explanation: He would like to build a robot that helps people who cannot walk.

parts.title: Robots in everyday life
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Many people think of robots as machines from films, but they are already part of everyday life. [1] They do jobs that are dull, dirty or dangerous for human beings.

In factories, robots build cars. [2] They can work all day and night without getting tired, and they rarely make a mistake.

In hospitals, some robots help doctors with difficult operations. [3] Their hands never shake, which makes the work safer for the patient.

At home, small robots clean floors and cut the grass. [4] Many people say that they have more free time now.

In the future, robots may even look after children and old people. [5] Others worry that people will become too lonely if machines do all the caring.
sentences: Some experts believe that this will be a great help for busy families.
The robot arm can be controlled from another room.
This is one reason why prices of cars have not risen so quickly.
There are about two million of them working across the world.
These machines are cheap enough for ordinary families to buy.
They were first invented more than two hundred years ago.

gaps.explanation: About two million of them work across the world, and the next sentence says what they do.
Robots help to keep the prices of cars down, and the next sentence says they work day and night.
The arm can be controlled from another room, and the next sentence says their hands never shake.
The machines are cheap enough for ordinary families, which leads to the idea of more free time.
Some experts believe it will help families, and "Others worry" gives the contrast.

parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Hi Sam, I am writing to tell you about our science project. Our teacher has asked us to make a model of a robot, [1] I have started to think about the design. I would like it to have two arms and a round head. It could be made [2] cardboard and plastic bottles. Could you bring the glue and the paint on Monday? I [3] to the shop yesterday, but they did not have the colours I needed. We have to finish the model [4] Friday, so we do not have much time. My dad can help us if we need him, because he is very good [5] making things. I think we will get a good mark if we work hard and do not leave everything until the [6] minute. See you soon, Nina

parts.title: Can machines think?
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Computers can do many things better than people. They can add up huge numbers in a second, and they never forget [1] they have learned. Some of them can even beat the best chess players in the world. However, many experts say that computers do not really think [2] we do. A computer follows rules that people have written, and it cannot understand why those rules exist. It also has no feelings. When you say something funny, a computer will not laugh unless somebody has [3] it to do so. Some scientists are trying to make machines that can learn by themselves, [4] watching and trying again, just like a child. Perhaps one day, there will be a machine that [5] truly intelligent. Nobody knows when this will happen, or [6] it will happen at all.

gaps.explanation: They never forget what they have learned: the object of forget.
Do not think like we do: a comparison.
Somebody has told it to do so: a past participle.
By watching and trying again: the means.
A machine that is truly intelligent: the verb to be.
Nobody knows if it will happen at all: an indirect question.

parts.title: A talk about a robot competition
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Good morning, everyone. I am Dara, the organiser of this year's school robot competition. It will take place on the twelfth of May in the main hall. Last year, twenty teams took part, and this year we hope for thirty. Each team can have up to four students. You have three months to build your robot, and you can use any materials you like, but the total cost must be under fifty pounds. The robot must be able to pick up a ball and carry it across the room. The judges will give points for speed, for strong design and for clever ideas. The winning team will receive a trophy and a free trip to the science museum. Please give me your team name by the end of next week. If you need help with the rules, ask Mr Evans, who teaches technology. Good luck, and have fun!

gaps.explanation: It will take place on the twelfth of May.

gaps.explanation: Each team can have up to four students.

gaps.explanation: The total cost must be under fifty pounds.

gaps.prompt: The robot has to carry a ___
gaps.explanation: It must be able to pick up a ball and carry it.

gaps.prompt: The winners will get a trip to the ___ museum
gaps.explanation: A free trip to the science museum.

parts.title: An interview with a robot designer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Dev, you design robots for a living. How did you become interested?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: When I was seven, my grandfather gave me a toy robot. I took it apart to see how it worked, and I never put it back together.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What kind of robots do you make today?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I make small ones that help in hospitals. They carry food and medicine to the rooms, so that nurses have more time for patients.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do people feel comfortable with them?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: At first, no. Some patients were afraid. So we gave the robots a friendly face and a gentle voice, and that changed everything.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the biggest problem in your work?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Making them safe. A robot must never hurt anyone, so we test each one for months before it leaves the factory.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Will robots take away people's jobs?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Some jobs will change, but I think new ones will appear. Somebody has to design, build and repair the machines.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do when you are not working?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I play the guitar. It is the one thing that no robot can do as well as a person with feelings.
